prompts.text: The silver chime in Bellwick Hall sounds at sunrise.
At daybreak, the metallic bell inside Bellwick Hall is rung.
A glass drum in Tervin Museum produces a low hum.
The deep buzzing sound at Tervin Museum comes from a drum made of glass.
Naro Station uses three short whistles to signal departure.
A train leaving Naro Station is announced by a trio of brief whistle blasts.
The echo in Kestrel Tunnel lasts four seconds.
A sound persists as a reflection for four seconds inside Kestrel Tunnel.
Mira Choir practices beside the old stone fountain.
The singers of Mira rehearse next to the weathered fountain of stone.
The violet moss on Arden Rock blooms only in autumn.
Only during fall does the purple moss of Arden Rock produce flowers.
A white cedar in Fenwick Garden was planted by Ada.
Ada is the person who put the pale cedar into the soil at Fenwick Garden.
The striped fern at Orlo Pond folds its fronds at noon.
At midday the banded fern growing by Orlo Pond closes its leaves.
Pavo Orchard grows six varieties of pear trees.
Six distinct kinds of pear are cultivated among the trees at Pavo Orchard.
The lantern vine in Oriel House climbs the east wall.
Along the eastern side of Oriel House grows the upward-creeping lantern vine.
The first frost in Velden Valley arrives in November.
November is when icy ground first appears in Velden Valley.
Clouds above Aster Ridge travel toward the southwest.
Over Aster Ridge the drifting clouds move in a southwesterly direction.
Rain at Mako Harbor usually begins after midnight.
The typical onset of precipitation in Mako Harbor is later than twelve at night.
A dry wind crosses Salten Plain every Thursday.
On Thursdays a breeze without moisture sweeps across Salten Plain.
The red weather flag at Brinn Pier warns of hail.
Hail is the hazard indicated by the crimson warning banner at Brinn Pier.
A bronze cup was discovered beneath Talo Bridge.
Excavators unearthed a drinking vessel made of bronze under Talo Bridge.
The Kori tablets were buried inside a clay jar.
A container of fired earth held the buried inscribed tablets from Kori.
A stone wheel at Aven Site dates to the fourth century.
The circular rock artifact at Aven Site originates in century four.
The oldest chamber at Miro Ruins faces north.
The earliest room in the ruins of Miro is oriented toward the northern direction.
An amber bead from Dalo Cave has seven carved lines.
Seven grooves are engraved on the yellow fossil-resin bead found at Dalo Cave.
The Orin rover sorts blue blocks before red blocks.
Blue pieces are classified ahead of red ones by the mobile robot named Orin.
A robot called Pex charges beside the loading dock.
The machine named Pex replenishes its battery next to the freight platform.
The Kiva arm places metal bolts into green trays.
Green containers receive the steel fasteners deposited by Kiva’s mechanical arm.
The Nelo drone returns home when its battery reaches twenty percent.
At one-fifth battery capacity, the flying machine Nelo heads back to base.
A sensor on Toma Bot detects warm pipes.
Heat from piping is what the detector mounted on Toma Bot identifies.
The navy scarf at Elin Workshop is woven from linen.
Flax fiber forms the dark-blue neck wrap produced at Elin Workshop.
A red carpet in Solin Hall contains nine golden knots.
Nine yellow-metal-colored knots decorate the crimson rug in Solin Hall.
Mora Tailor uses a copper needle for heavy cloth.
Thick fabric is stitched by Mora Tailor with a sewing needle made of copper.
The green banner in Elda Square was dyed with leaves.
Plant foliage provided the color of the verdant flag hanging in Elda Square.
Taro Mill makes wool blankets in the winter season.
During the cold months, Taro Mill produces coverings from sheep fleece.
The blue lens in Sora Lab enlarges distant objects.
Faraway items look bigger through the azure optical glass at Sora Lab.
A mirror in Vale Observatory points toward the west.
The reflective panel at Vale Observatory is oriented in a westerly direction.
The prism at Orla School separates sunlight into colors.
Sunshine is divided into a spectrum by the transparent wedge at Orla School.
A lamp in Iven Gallery projects a square shadow.
The light fixture in Iven Gallery casts a shadow shaped like a quadrilateral with equal sides.
The narrow aperture in Fenor Camera admits less light.
Only a smaller quantity of illumination passes through Fenor Camera’s tiny opening.
The Daren dialect uses a rising tone for questions.
Interrogative sentences in the Daren speech variety end with an upward pitch.
The old Ruma script writes numbers from right to left.
Numerals are inscribed starting on the right in the ancient writing system of Ruma.
A glossary at Vero Library lists forty plant names.
Forty botanical terms are catalogued in the vocabulary reference at Vero Library.
The Peli language marks past tense with a suffix.
An ending attached to the word indicates earlier time in Peli grammar.
The translation contest at Loma School lasts two hours.
Competitors at Loma School have a duration of 120 minutes to translate text.
